(1) We can obtain a CDH-based signature scheme with $$\mathbf {\mathcal {O}}(1)$$O(\mathcal{O}(1)) and $$\mathbf{\mathcal {O}(\mathit{log}(k))}$$O(\mathit{O}(\mathcal{log}(k))) elements in signatures and verification keys, respectively, from the CDH assumption in pairing-friendly group.
we show how to combine several instances of only mildly secure signature schemes to obtain a fully-secure signature scheme.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to combine instances of mildly secure signature schemes to obtain a fully (strongly unforgeable) secure signature scheme.
a very general and interesting question: Can we combine several instances of a mild security assumption to obtain a fully-secure signature scheme?
the question how to combine several instances of a mildly secure signature to obtain a fully-secure signature scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we provide a number of new signature schemes that are more compact and efficient than existing ones, but at the price of a larger loss in the security proof.
we obtain the first CDH-based scheme which is fully secure and provides compact signatures, and the first RSA-based scheme which is efficient and fully secure.
we have found a new way of constructing very efficient signature schemes from standard assumptions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in all cases, we can achieve the security level of the best known schemes with signature and verification key sizes that are significantly smaller than the ones obtained from the best known schemes.
for the first time, we can construct very efficient and standard-compliant signature schemes from CDH, RSA, and SIS, respectively, with only a polynomial loss in the security reductions.
, for any of our constructions, we can trade off the security reduction for signature/verification key size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we provide a new and very flexible technique to obtain very compact signatures.
we provide a new and very efficient way to combine instances of a mild signature notion.

, for a wide range of standard assumptions, we can construct very efficient signature schemes with compact keys by using our technique of combining several instances of a mildly secure building block.
